learning: Iteration 6 showed the 16 mm footprint gave no clear gain (62.13 vs 62.87), so sensing is no longer the limit. Yaw authority is the next lever. Narrower track raises yaw gain by about 25 percent at the same kp, so slalom oscillation is the main risk to watch.
notes: Iteration 5 geometry with the 12 mm footprint restored and wheel_track narrowed from 0.10 to 0.08 m. The controller is identical to iteration 5, so the race isolates yaw authority.
rationale: Iteration 6 (16 mm footprints) scored 62.13, below iteration 5's 62.87. The oval gained nothing further (progress 0.168 vs 0.175), the s-bend was flat or slightly down (0.165 to 0.165 progress, max_error 0.0619), and the slalom gained about 0.8 but the aggregate still fell. The footprint change does not clearly help, so I revert sensor_size to 0.012 m, the best measured footprint. The seven-sensor row at +/-0.06 m, y = 0.07 m, is kept, since span removed oval line loss in iteration 5 (0 events, progress 0.175). Every run still ends with one line-loss event on the s-bend and slalom and max_error about 0.062 m, which is set by the fixed 0.06 m off-track floor. The Builder's requested yaw-authority test is the remaining drivetrain lever, and drivetrain changes have so far been small (iteration 1 moved the score by only 0.14). I narrow wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.08 m, which raises yaw per PWM count by about 25 percent. I keep kp at 1.25, kd at 0.25, ki at 0, base_speed at 1.5 and the iteration 5 weights, so the only change from iteration 5 is wheel_track, which isolates the yaw-authority effect. I do not scale kp down to hold effective gain, because the test is precisely whether extra yaw authority lets the controller hold the 0.06 m floor. Mass (0.6 kg), wheel_radius (0.03 m) and body (0.18 x 0.12 m) stay fixed. Expected: line_loss_events trending toward 0 on the s-bend and slalom, max_error below 0.06 m, and progress above the iteration 5 values (0.165 s-bend, 0.110 slalom). Risk: the higher yaw gain may raise slalom steering_oscillation above about 0.16, in which case the next step is wheel_track 0.09 m.
